content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.english: 30:5 Thou wilt bring me out of this snare, which they have hidden for me: * for thou art my protector.

segments.t: Edúces me de láqueo hoc, quem abscondérunt mihi: * quóniam tu es protéctor meus.

content.latin: 30:6 In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: * redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.

segments.t: In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: * redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.

segments.t: Odísti observántes vanitátes, * supervácue.

segments.t: Factus sum tamquam vas pérditum: * quóniam audívi vituperatiónem multórum commorántium in circúitu.

content.latin: 30:14 In eo dum convenírent simul advérsum me, * accípere ánimam meam consiliáti sunt.
content.english: 30:14 While they assembled together against me, * they consulted to take away my life.

segments.t: In eo dum convenírent simul advérsum me, * accípere ánimam meam consiliáti sunt.

content.latin: 30:15 Ego autem in te sperávi, Dómine: * dixi: Deus meus es tu: in mánibus tuis sortes meæ.
content.english: 30:15 But I have put my trust in thee, O Lord: * I said: Thou art my God. My lots are in thy hands.

segments.t: Ego autem in te sperávi, Dómine: * dixi: Deus meus es tu: in mánibus tuis sortes meæ.

content.latin: 30:16 Éripe me de manu inimicórum meórum, * et a persequéntibus me.
content.english: 30:16 Deliver me out of the hands of my enemies; * and from them that persecute me

segments.t: Éripe me de manu inimicórum meórum, * et a persequéntibus me.

content.latin: 30:17 Illústra fáciem tuam super servum tuum, salvum me fac in misericórdia tua: * Dómine, non confúndar, quóniam invocávi te.
content.english: 30:17 Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; save me in thy mercy. * Let me not be confounded, O Lord, for I have called upon thee.

segments.t: Illústra fáciem tuam super servum tuum, salvum me fac in misericórdia tua: * Dómine, non confúndar, quóniam invocávi te.

content.latin: 30:18 Erubéscant ímpii, et deducántur in inférnum: * muta fiant lábia dolósa.
content.english: 30:18 Let the wicked be ashamed, and be brought down to hell. * Let deceitful lips be made dumb.

segments.t: Erubéscant ímpii, et deducántur in inférnum: * muta fiant lábia dolósa.

content.latin: 30:19 Quæ loquúntur advérsus iustum iniquitátem: * in supérbia, et in abusióne.
content.english: 30:19 Which speak iniquity against the just, * with pride and abuse.

segments.t: Quæ loquúntur advérsus iustum iniquitátem: * in supérbia, et in abusióne.

content.latin: 30:20 Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ, Dómine, * quam abscondísti timéntibus te.
content.english: 30:20 How great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord, * which thou hast hidden for them that fear thee!

segments.t: Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ, Dómine, * quam abscondísti timéntibus te.

content.latin: 30:20 Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te, * in conspéctu filiórum hóminum.
content.english: 30:20 Which thou hast wrought for them that hope in thee, * in the sight of the sons of men.

segments.t: Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te, * in conspéctu filiórum hóminum.

content.latin: 30:21 Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ * a conturbatióne hóminum.
content.english: 30:21 Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy face, * from the disturbance of men.

segments.t: Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ * a conturbatióne hóminum.

content.latin: 30:21 Próteges eos in tabernáculo tuo * a contradictióne linguárum.
content.english: 30:21 Thou shalt protect them in thy tabernacle * from the contradiction of tongues.

segments.t: Próteges eos in tabernáculo tuo * a contradictióne linguárum.

content.latin: 30:22 Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam mirificávit misericórdiam suam mihi in civitáte muníta.
content.english: 30:22 Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath shewn his wonderful mercy to me in a fortified city.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam mirificávit misericórdiam suam mihi in civitáte muníta.

content.latin: 30:23 Ego autem dixi in excéssu mentis meæ: * Proiéctus sum a fácie oculórum tuórum.
content.english: 30:23 But I said in the excess of my mind: * I am cast away from before thy eyes.

segments.t: Ego autem dixi in excéssu mentis meæ: * Proiéctus sum a fácie oculórum tuórum.

content.latin: 30:23 Ídeo exaudísti vocem oratiónis meæ, * dum clamárem ad te.
content.english: 30:23 Therefore thou hast heard the voice of my prayer, * when I cried to thee.

segments.t: Ídeo exaudísti vocem oratiónis meæ, * dum clamárem ad te.

content.latin: 30:24 Dilígite Dóminum omnes sancti eius: * quóniam veritátem requíret Dóminus, et retríbuet abundánter faciéntibus supérbiam.
content.english: 30:24 O love the Lord, all ye his saints: * for the Lord will require truth, and will repay them abundantly that act proudly.

segments.t: Dilígite Dóminum omnes sancti eius: * quóniam veritátem requíret Dóminus, et retríbuet abundánter faciéntibus supérbiam.

content.latin: 30:25 Viríliter ágite, et confortétur cor vestrum, * omnes, qui sperátis in Dómino.
content.english: 30:25 Do ye manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, * all ye that hope in the Lord.

segments.t: Viríliter ágite, et confortétur cor vestrum, * omnes, qui sperátis in Dómino.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Defécit in dolóre vita mea, et anni mei in gemítibus.
content.english: Ant. My life is spent with grief, and my years with sighing.

segments.t: Ant.
Defécit in dolóre vita mea, et anni mei in gemítibus.

content.latin: ℣. Regína Mártyrum, ora pro nobis.
content.english: ℣. Pray for us, O Queen of Martyrs.

segments.t: Regína Mártyrum, ora pro nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Quæ iuxta crucem Iesu constitísti.
content.english: ℟. Who didst stand by the Cross of Jesus.

segments.t: Quæ iuxta crucem Iesu constitísti.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: De Ieremía Prophéta
content.english: Lesson from the book of Lamentations

content.latin: 2 (Beth) Plorans plorávit in nocte, et lácrimæ eius in maxíllis eius: non est qui consolétur eam ex ómnibus caris eius: omnes amíci eius sprevérunt eam, et facti sunt ei inimíci.
content.english: 2 Weeping she hath wept in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks: there is none to comfort her among all them that were dear to her: all her friends have despised her, and are become her enemies.

segments.t: (Beth) Plorans plorávit in nocte, et lácrimæ eius in maxíllis eius: non est qui consolétur eam ex ómnibus caris eius: omnes amíci eius sprevérunt eam, et facti sunt ei inimíci.

content.latin: 20 (Res) Vide, Dómine, quóniam tríbulor, conturbátus est venter meus, subvérsum est cor meum in memetípsa, quóniam amaritúdine plena sum. Foris intérfecit gládius, et domi mors símilis est.
content.english: 20 Behold, O Lord, for I am in distress, my bowels are troubled: my heart is turned within me, for I am full of bitterness: abroad the sword destroyeth, and at home there is death alike.

segments.t: (Res) Vide, Dómine, quóniam tríbulor, conturbátus est venter meus, subvérsum est cor meum in memetípsa, quóniam amaritúdine plena sum. Foris intérfecit gládius, et domi mors símilis est.

content.latin: 21 (Sin) Audiérunt quia ingemísco ego, et non est qui consolétur me.
content.english: 21 They have heard that I sigh, and there is none to comfort me.

segments.t: (Sin) Audiérunt quia ingemísco ego, et non est qui consolétur me.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Símeon, vir iustus et timorátus, dixit ad Maríam:
content.english: ℟. There was a man whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout; and he said unto Mary

segments.t: Símeon, vir iustus et timorátus, dixit ad Maríam:

content.latin: * Tuam ipsíus ánimam pertransíbit gládius.
content.english: * Yea, a sword shall pierce through thine own soul also.

content.latin: ℣. Ne vocétis me pulchram, sed amáram, quia amaritúdine valde replévit me Omnípotens.
content.english: ℣. Call me not My-pleasantness, but call me Embittered, for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.

segments.t: Ne vocétis me pulchram, sed amáram, quia amaritúdine valde replévit me Omnípotens.

content.latin: ℟. Tuam ipsíus ánimam pertransíbit gládius.
content.english: ℟. Yea, a sword shall pierce through thine own soul also.

segments.t: Tuam ipsíus ánimam pertransíbit gládius.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 13 (Mem) Cui comparábo te? vel cui assimilábo te, fília Ierúsalem? cui exæquábo te, et consolábor te, virgo fília Sion? Magna est enim velut mare contrítio tua: quis medébitur tui?
content.english: 13 To what shall I compare thee? or to what shall I liken thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? to what shall I equal thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Sion? for great as the sea is thy destruction: who shall heal thee?

segments.t: (Mem) Cui comparábo te? vel cui assimilábo te, fília Ierúsalem? cui exæquábo te, et consolábor te, virgo fília Sion? Magna est enim velut mare contrítio tua: quis medébitur tui?

content.latin: 15 (Samech) Plausérunt super te mánibus omnes transeúntes per viam: sibilavérunt, et movérunt caput suum super fíliam Ierúsalem: Hǽccine est urbs, dicéntes, perfécti decóris, gáudium univérsæ terræ?
content.english: 15 All they that passed by the way have clapped their hands at thee: they have hissed, and wagged their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying: Is this the city of perfect beauty, the joy of all the earth?

segments.t: (Samech) Plausérunt super te mánibus omnes transeúntes per viam: sibilavérunt, et movérunt caput suum super fíliam Ierúsalem: Hǽccine est urbs, dicéntes, perfécti decóris, gáudium univérsæ terræ?

content.latin: 16 (Phe) Aperuérunt super te os suum omnes inimíci tui, sibilavérunt et fremuérunt déntibus, et dixérunt: Devorábimus.
content.english: 16 All thy enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they have hissed, and gnashed with the teeth, and have said: We will swallow her up.

segments.t: (Phe) Aperuérunt super te os suum omnes inimíci tui, sibilavérunt et fremuérunt déntibus, et dixérunt: Devorábimus.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem eius, et fuge in Ægýptum;
content.english: ℟. Arise, and take the young Child and His Mother, and flee into Egypt;

segments.t: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem eius, et fuge in Ægýptum;

content.latin: * Et esto ibi usque dum dicam tibi.
content.english: * And be thou there until I bring thee word.

content.latin: ℣. Vocávi fílium meum ex Ægýpto, ut véniat salus in Israël.
content.english: ℣. Out of Egypt have I called My Son, that salvation may come unto Israel.

segments.t: Vocávi fílium meum ex Ægýpto, ut véniat salus in Israël.

content.latin: ℟. Et esto ibi usque dum dicam tibi.
content.english: ℟. And be thou there until I bring thee word.

segments.t: Et esto ibi usque dum dicam tibi.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 17 (Ain) Fecit Dóminus quæ cogitávit, complévit sermónem suum quem præcéperat a diébus antíquis: destrúxit et non pepércit, et lætificávit super te inimícum et exaltávit cornu hóstium tuórum.
content.english: 17 The Lord hath done that which he purposed, he hath fulfilled his word, which he commanded in the days of old: he hath destroyed, and hath not spared, and he hath caused the enemy to rejoice over thee, and hath set up the horn of thy adversaries.

segments.t: (Ain) Fecit Dóminus quæ cogitávit, complévit sermónem suum quem præcéperat a diébus antíquis: destrúxit et non pepércit, et lætificávit super te inimícum et exaltávit cornu hóstium tuórum.

content.latin: 18 (Sade) Clamávit cor eórum ad Dóminum super muros fíliæ Sion: Deduc quasi torréntem lácrimas per diem et noctem; non des réquiem tibi, neque táceat pupílla óculi tui.
content.english: 18 Their heart cried to the Lord upon the walls of the daughter of Sion: Let tears run down like a torrent day and night: give thyself no rest, and let not the apple of thy eye cease.

segments.t: (Sade) Clamávit cor eórum ad Dóminum super muros fíliæ Sion: Deduc quasi torréntem lácrimas per diem et noctem; non des réquiem tibi, neque táceat pupílla óculi tui.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.english: ℟. Son, why hast Thou thus dealt with us?

segments.t: Fili, quid fecísti nobis sic?

content.latin: * Ego et pater tuus * Doléntes quærebámus te.
content.english: * I and thy father have sought thee sorrowing.

content.latin: ℣. Quid est quod me quærebátis? In his quæ Patris mei sunt, opórtet me esse.
content.english: ℣. How is it that ye sought Me? Wist ye not that I must be about My Father's business?

segments.t: Quid est quod me quærebátis? In his quæ Patris mei sunt, opórtet me esse.

content.latin: ℟. Ego et pater tuus.
content.english: ℟. I and thy Father

segments.t: Ego et pater tuus.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. Have sought thee sorrowing.

segments.t: Doléntes quærebámus te.

content.english: Nocturn II

content.latin: Ant. Factum est cor meum * tamquam cera liquéscens in médio ventris mei.
content.english: Ant. My heart is like * melting wax in the midst of my bowels.

segments.t: Ant.
Factum est cor meum * tamquam cera liquéscens in médio ventris mei.

content.latin: Psalmus 21 [4]
content.english: Psalm 21 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 21

content.latin: 21:2 Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me: quare me dereliquísti? * longe a salúte mea verba delictórum meórum.
content.english: 21:2 O God my God, look upon me: why hast thou forsaken me? * Far from my salvation are the words of my sins.

segments.t: Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me: quare me dereliquísti? * longe a salúte mea verba delictórum meórum.

content.latin: 21:3 Deus meus, clamábo per diem, et non exáudies: * et nocte, et non ad insipiéntiam mihi.
content.english: 21:3 O my God, I shall cry by day, and thou wilt not hear: * and by night, and it shall not be reputed as folly in me.

segments.t: Deus meus, clamábo per diem, et non exáudies: * et nocte, et non ad insipiéntiam mihi.

content.latin: 21:4 Tu autem in sancto hábitas, * laus Israël.
content.english: 21:4 But thou dwellest in the holy place, * the praise of Israel.

segments.t: Tu autem in sancto hábitas, * laus Israël.

content.latin: 21:5 In te speravérunt patres nostri: * speravérunt, et liberásti eos.
content.english: 21:5 In thee have our fathers hoped: * they have hoped, and thou hast delivered them.

segments.t: In te speravérunt patres nostri: * speravérunt, et liberásti eos.

content.latin: 21:6 Ad te clamavérunt, et salvi facti sunt: * in te speravérunt, et non sunt confúsi.
content.english: 21:6 They cried to thee, and they were saved: * they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.

segments.t: Ad te clamavérunt, et salvi facti sunt: * in te speravérunt, et non sunt confúsi.

content.latin: 21:7 Ego autem sum vermis, et non homo: * oppróbrium hóminum, et abiéctio plebis.
content.english: 21:7 But I am a worm, and no man: * the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people.

segments.t: Ego autem sum vermis, et non homo: * oppróbrium hóminum, et abiéctio plebis.

content.latin: 21:8 Omnes vidéntes me, derisérunt me: * locúti sunt lábiis, et movérunt caput.
content.english: 21:8 All they that saw me have laughed me to scorn: * they have spoken with the lips, and wagged the head.

segments.t: Omnes vidéntes me, derisérunt me: * locúti sunt lábiis, et movérunt caput.

content.latin: 21:9 Sperávit in Dómino, erípiat eum: * salvum fáciat eum, quóniam vult eum.
content.english: 21:9 He hoped in the Lord, let him deliver him: * let him save him, seeing he delighteth in him.

segments.t: Sperávit in Dómino, erípiat eum: * salvum fáciat eum, quóniam vult eum.

content.latin: 21:10 Quóniam tu es, qui extraxísti me de ventre: * spes mea ab ubéribus matris meæ. In te proiéctus sum ex útero:
content.english: 21:10 For thou art he that hast drawn me out of the womb: * my hope from the breasts of my mother. I was cast upon thee from the womb.

segments.t: Quóniam tu es, qui extraxísti me de ventre: * spes mea ab ubéribus matris meæ. In te proiéctus sum ex útero:

content.latin: 21:11 De ventre matris meæ Deus meus es tu, * ne discésseris a me:
content.english: 21:11 From my mother’s womb thou art my God, * depart not from me.

segments.t: De ventre matris meæ Deus meus es tu, * ne discésseris a me:

content.latin: 21:12 Quóniam tribulátio próxima est: * quóniam non est qui ádiuvet.
content.english: 21:12 For tribulation is very near: * for there is none to help me.

segments.t: Quóniam tribulátio próxima est: * quóniam non est qui ádiuvet.

content.latin: 21:13 Circumdedérunt me vítuli multi: * tauri pingues obsedérunt me.
content.english: 21:13 Many calves have surrounded me: * fat bulls have besieged me.

segments.t: Circumdedérunt me vítuli multi: * tauri pingues obsedérunt me.

content.latin: 21:14 Aperuérunt super me os suum, * sicut leo rápiens et rúgiens.
content.english: 21:14 They have opened their mouths against me, * as a lion ravening and roaring.

segments.t: Aperuérunt super me os suum, * sicut leo rápiens et rúgiens.

content.latin: 21:15 Sicut aqua effúsus sum: * et dispérsa sunt ómnia ossa mea.
content.english: 21:15 I am poured out like water; * and all my bones are scattered.

segments.t: Sicut aqua effúsus sum: * et dispérsa sunt ómnia ossa mea.

content.latin: 21:15 Factum est cor meum tamquam cera liquéscens * in médio ventris mei.
content.english: 21:15 My heart is become like wax melting * in the midst of my bowels.

segments.t: Factum est cor meum tamquam cera liquéscens * in médio ventris mei.

content.latin: 21:17 Fodérunt manus meas et pedes meos: * dinumeravérunt ómnia ossa mea.

segments.t: Fodérunt manus meas et pedes meos: * dinumeravérunt ómnia ossa mea.

content.latin: 21:18 Ipsi vero consideravérunt et inspexérunt me: * divisérunt sibi vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.

content.latin: 21:20 Tu autem, Dómine, ne elongáveris auxílium tuum a me: * ad defensiónem meam cónspice.
content.english: 21:20 But thou, O Lord, remove not thy help to a distance from me; * look towards my defence.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, ne elongáveris auxílium tuum a me: * ad defensiónem meam cónspice.

content.english: 21:21 Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword: * my only one from the hand of the dog.

segments.t: Qui timétis Dóminum, laudáte eum: * univérsum semen Iacob, glorificáte eum.

segments.t: Apud te laus mea in ecclésia magna: * vota mea reddam in conspéctu timéntium eum.

content.latin: 21:27 Edent páuperes, et saturabúntur: et laudábunt Dóminum qui requírunt eum: * vivent corda eórum in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 21:27 The poor shall eat and shall be filled: and they shall praise the Lord that seek him: * their hearts shall live for ever and ever.

content.english: 21:30 All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and have adored: * all they that go down to the earth shall fall before him.

segments.t: Manducavérunt et adoravérunt omnes pingues terræ: * in conspéctu eius cadent omnes qui descéndunt in terram.

content.latin: 21:31 Et ánima mea illi vivet: * et semen meum sérviet ipsi.
content.english: 21:31 And to him my soul shall live: * and my seed shall serve him.

content.latin: 55:2 Miserére mei, Deus, quóniam conculcávit me homo: * tota die impúgnans tribulávit me.
content.english: 55:2 Have mercy on me, O God, for man hath trodden me under foot; * all the day long he hath afflicted me fighting against me.

segments.t: Miserére mei, Deus, quóniam conculcávit me homo: * tota die impúgnans tribulávit me.

content.latin: 55:3 Conculcavérunt me inimíci mei tota die: * quóniam multi bellántes advérsum me.
content.english: 55:3 My enemies have trodden on me all the day long; * for they are many that make war against me.

segments.t: Conculcavérunt me inimíci mei tota die: * quóniam multi bellántes advérsum me.

content.english: 55:4 From the height of the day I shall fear: * but I will trust in thee.

segments.t: Ab altitúdine diéi timébo: * ego vero in te sperábo.

content.latin: 55:5 In Deo laudábo sermónes meos, in Deo sperávi: * non timébo quid fáciat mihi caro.
content.english: 55:5 In God I will praise my words, in God I have put my trust: * I will not fear what flesh can do against me.

content.english: 55:6 All the day long they detested my words: * all their thoughts were against me unto evil.

content.english: 55:7 They will dwell and hide themselves: * they will watch my heel.

content.english: 55:8 As they have waited for my soul, for nothing shalt thou save them: * in thy anger thou shalt break the people in pieces.

segments.t: Sicut sustinuérunt ánimam meam, pro níhilo salvos fácies illos: * in ira pópulos confrínges.

content.latin: Martýrium Vírginis tam in Simeónis prophetía, quam in ipsa Domínicæ passiónis história commendátur. Pósitus est hic (ait sanctus senex de púero Iesu) in signum cui contradicétur; et tuam ipsíus ánimam (ad Maríam autem dicébat) pertransíbit gládius. Vere tuam, o beáta Mater, ánimam pertransívit. Alióquin non nisi eam pertránsiens, carnem Fílii tui penetráret. Et quidem posteáquam emísit spíritum tuus ille Iesus, ipsíus plane non áttigit ánimam crudélis láncea, quæ ipsíus apéruit latus, sed tuam útique ánimam pertransívit. Ipsíus nimírum ánima iam ibi non erat, sed tua plane inde nequíbat avélli.
content.english: The Martyrdom of the Virgin is set before us, not only in the prophecy of Simeon, but also in the story itself of the Lord's Passion. The holy old man said of the Child Jesus Luke ii. 34, Behold, this Child is set for the fall and the rising again of many in Israel; and for a sign which shall be spoken against; yea, said he unto Mary, a sword shall pierce through thine own soul also Even so, O Blessed Mother! The sword did indeed pierce through thy soul! for nought could pierce the Body of thy Son, nor pierce thy soul likewise. Yea, and when this Jesus of thine had given up the ghost, and the bloody spear could torture Him no more, thy soul winced as it pierced His dead Side His Own Soul might leave Him, but thine could not.

content.latin: Tuam ergo pertransívit ánimam vis dolóris, ut plusquam Mártyrem non immérito prædicémus, in qua nimírum corpóreæ sensum passiónis excésserit compassiónis afféctus. An non tibi plusquam gládius fuit sermo ille, revéra pertránsiens ánimam, et pertíngens usque ad divisiónem ánimæ et spíritus: Múlier, ecce fílius tuus? O commutatiónem! Ioánnes tibi pro Iesu tráditur, servus pro Dómino, discípulus pro Magístro, fílius Zebedǽi pro Fílio Dei, homo purus pro Deo vero. Quómodo non tuam affectuosíssimam ánimam pertransíret hæc audítio, quando et nostra, licet sáxea, licet férrea péctora, sola recordátio scindit?
content.english: The sword of sorrow pierced through thy soul, so that we may truly call thee more than martyr, in whom the love, that made thee suffer along with thy Son, wrung thy heart more bitterly than any pang of bodily pain could do. Did not that word of His indeed pierce through thy soul, sharper than any two-edged sword, even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, Heb. iv. 12, Woman, behold thy son! John xix. 26. O what a change to thee! Thou art given John for Jesus, the servant for his Lord, the disciple for his master, the son of Zebedee for the Son of God, a mere man for Very God. O how keenly must the hearing of those words have pierced through thy most loving soul, when even our hearts, stony, iron, as they are, are wrung at the memory thereof only!

content.latin: Non mirémini, fratres, quod María Martyr in ánima fuísse dicátur. Mirétur qui non memínerit se audivísse Paulum inter máxima géntium crímina memorántem, quod sine affectióne fuíssent. Longe id fuit a Maríæ viscéribus, longe sit a sérvulis eius. Sed forte quis dicat: Numquid non eum præscíerat moritúrum? Et indubitánter. Numquid non sperábat contínuo resurrectúrum? Et fidéliter. Super hæc dóluit crucifíxum? Et veheménter. Alióquin quisnam tu, frater, aut unde tibi hæc sapiéntia, ut miréris plus Maríæ Fílium patiéntem? Ille étiam mori córpore pótuit; ista cómmori corde non pótuit? Fecit illud cáritas, qua maiórem nemo hábuit; fecit et hoc cáritas, cui post illam símilis áltera non fuit.
content.english: Marvel not, my brethren, that Mary should be called a Martyr in spirit. He indeed may marvel who remembereth not what Paul saith, naming the greater sins of the Gentiles, that they were without natural affection, Rom. i. 31. Far other were the bowels of Mary, and far other may those of her servants be! But some man perchance will say Did she not know that He was to die? Yea, without doubt, she knew it. Did she not hope that He was soon to rise again? Yea, she most faithfully hoped it. And did she still mourn because He was crucified? Yea, bitterly. But who art thou, my brother, or whence hast thou such wisdom, to marvel less that the Son of Mary suffered than that Mary suffered with Him? He could die in the Body, and could not she die with Him in her heart? His was the deed of that Love, greater than which hath no man John xv. 13; hers, of a love, like to which hath no man, save He.

content.latin: Stabat iuxta crucem Mater, et, fugiéntibus viris, stabat intrépida. Vidéte utrum pudórem mutáre potúerit Mater Iesu, quæ ánimum non mutávit. Spectábat piis óculis Fílii vúlnera, per quæ sciébat ómnibus futúram redemptiónem. Spectábat non degéneri mater spectáculo, quæ non metúerat peremptórem. Pendébat in cruce Fílius, Mater se persecutóribus offerébat.
content.english: There stood by the Cross His Mother. Men had forsaken Him, but she stood there fearless. Behold how the Mother of Jesus could break through her shrinking modesty, but could not belie her heart. With the eyes of a mother's love she gazed upon the Wounds of her Son, those Wounds through Which she knew that redemption for all mankind was flowing. The Mother, who feared not the executioners, was able to endure the sight of their work. Her Son was hanging upon the Cross, and she braved His tormentors.

content.latin: María Mater Dómini ante crucem Fílii stabat. Nullus me hoc dócuit, nisi sanctus Ioánnes Evangelísta. Mundum álii concússum in passióne Dómini conscripsérunt, cælum ténebris obdúctum, refugísse solem, in paradísum latrónem, sed post piam confessiónem, recéptum. Ioánnes dócuit, quod álii non docuérunt, quemádmodum in cruce pósitus Matrem appelláverit. Pluris putátur quod victor suppliciórum pietátis offícia Matri exhibébat, quam quod regnum cæléste donábat. Nam si religiósum est quod latróni donátur vénia, multo uberióris pietátis est quod a Fílio Mater tanto afféctu honorátur.
content.english: Mary, the Mother of the Lord, stood by the Cross of her Son. My only informant of this fact is the holy Evangelist John. Others have written that when the Lord suffered, the earth quaked, the heavens were veiled in darkness, the sun was hidden, and the thief received, after a good confession, the promise of Paradise. John hath taught us what the others have not taught us. Upon the Cross He called her Mother. It is reckoned (by John) a greater thing that in the moment of triumph over agony, He should have discharged the watchful duty of a Son to His Mother, than that He should have made gift of the kingdom of heaven. For if it be a sacred thing to have forgiven the thief, this so great kindness of the Son to the Mother is to be worshipped as the outcome of a tenderer and more touching love.

content.latin: Ecce, inquit, fílius tuus: ecce mater tua. Testabátur de cruce Christus, et inter matrem atque discípulum dividébat pietátis offícia. Condébat Dóminus non solum públicum, sed étiam domésticum testaméntum: et hoc eius testaméntum signábat Ioánnes, dignus tanto testatóre testis. Bonum testaméntum, non pecúniæ, sed vitæ ætérnæ; quod non atraménto scriptum est, sed Spíritu Dei vivi, qui ait: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: Behold, saith the Lord, thy son: Behold thy Mother! Christ bore witness from the Cross, and divided the offices of his tender love between his Mother and his disciple. Thus doth the Lord give us a testament, not only of his love for souls, but also of his natural affection. Moreover, the testimony which John doth give us concerning this same testament, is a worthy testimony to the original Testator himself. It is a good testament, not of earthly riches, but of eternal life, written not in ink, but in the Spirit of the living God, who speaketh of such testimony in the Psalms, saying: My tongue is the pen of a ready writer.

segments.t: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

segments.t: Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.

content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

segments.t: In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.

segments.t: Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.

content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

segments.t: Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.

content.latin: Deus, in cuius passióne, secúndum Simeónis prophetíam, dulcíssimam ánimam gloriósæ Vírginis et Matris Maríæ dolóris gládius pertransívit: concéde propítius; ut, qui dolóres eius venerándo recólimus, passiónis tuæ efféctum felícem consequámur:

content.latin: 24:1 Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam.
content.english: 24:1 To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul: * In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.

segments.t: Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam.

content.latin: 24:3 Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: * étenim univérsi, qui sústinent te, non confundéntur.
content.english: 24:3 Neither let my enemies laugh at me: * for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.

segments.t: Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: * étenim univérsi, qui sústinent te, non confundéntur.

content.latin: 24:4 Confundántur omnes iníqua agéntes * supervácue.
content.english: 24:4 Let all them be confounded that act unjust things * without cause.

segments.t: Confundántur omnes iníqua agéntes * supervácue.

content.latin: 24:4 Vias tuas, Dómine, demónstra mihi: * et sémitas tuas édoce me.

segments.t: Vias tuas, Dómine, demónstra mihi: * et sémitas tuas édoce me.

content.latin: 24:5 Dírige me in veritáte tua, et doce me: * quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus, et te sustínui tota die.
content.english: 24:5 Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; * for thou art God my Saviour; and on thee have I waited all the day long.

segments.t: Dírige me in veritáte tua, et doce me: * quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus, et te sustínui tota die.

content.latin: 24:6 Reminíscere miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, * et misericordiárum tuárum, quæ a sǽculo sunt.
content.english: 24:6 Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; * and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world.

segments.t: Reminíscere miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, * et misericordiárum tuárum, quæ a sǽculo sunt.

content.latin: 24:7 Delícta iuventútis meæ, * et ignorántias meas ne memíneris.

segments.t: Delícta iuventútis meæ, * et ignorántias meas ne memíneris.

content.latin: 24:7 Secúndum misericórdiam tuam meménto mei tu: * propter bonitátem tuam, Dómine.

content.latin: Chalcedóne natális sanctæ Euphémiæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Prisco Procónsule, torménta, cárceres, vérbera, arguménta rotárum, ignes, póndera lápidum, béstias, plagas virgárum, serras acútas, sartágines ignítas pro Christo superávit. Sed, rursus in theátrum ad béstias ducta, ibi, cum orásset ad Dóminum ut iam spíritum suum suscíperet, una ex iis morsum sancto córpori infigénte, céteris pedes eius lambéntibus, immaculátum spíritum Deo réddidit.
content.english: At Chalcedon, the holy Virgin and martyr Euphemia. Under the Emperor Diocletian and the Proconsul Priscus, she overcame for Christ's sake torture, imprisonment, stripes, wheels, fire, stones, beasts, rods, sharp saws, and hot metal. When she was again cast to the beasts in the theatre, she prayed the Lord to take her spirit to Himself, and then one of them bit her sacred body, while the rest licked her feet, and she resigned her soul without spot to God.

content.english: At Rome, the holy martyrs Lucy, a noble matron, and Geminian, whom the Emperor Diocletian, after they had suffered grievously and long been tormented, and had thus gained a noble victory by martyrdom, commanded to be slain with the sword.

Eius corpus, póstea Romam translátum, in Ecclésia sanctórum Silvéstri et Martíni cónditum fuit. Ipsíus tamen festívitas prídie Idus Novémbris celebrátur.

segments.t: Iustítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: * veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.

content.latin: 39:11 Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.
content.english: 39:11 I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth * from a great council.

segments.t: Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.

content.latin: 39:12 Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
content.english: 39:12 Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: * thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.

content.latin: 39:13 Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
content.english: 39:13 For evils without number have surrounded me; * my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.

segments.t: Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.

content.latin: 39:13 Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.
content.english: 39:13 They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: * and my heart hath forsaken me.

segments.t: Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.

content.latin: 39:14 Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me réspice.
content.english: 39:14 Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: * look down, O Lord, to help me.

segments.t: Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me réspice.

Psalmus 39(15-18)

content.latin: 39:15 Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, * ut áuferant eam.
content.english: 39:15 Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul * to take it away.

segments.t: Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, * ut áuferant eam.

content.latin: 39:15 Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, * qui volunt mihi mala.
content.english: 39:15 Let them be turned backward and be ashamed * that desire evils to me.

segments.t: Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, * qui volunt mihi mala.

content.latin: 39:16 Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
content.english: 39:16 Let them immediately bear their confusion, * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

segments.t: Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.

content.latin: 39:17 Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
content.english: 39:17 Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

segments.t: Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.

content.latin: 39:18 Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
content.english: 39:18 But I am a beggar and poor: * the Lord is careful for me.

segments.t: Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.

content.latin: 39:18 Adiútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
content.english: 39:18 Thou art my helper and my protector: * O my God, be not slack.

segments.t: Adiútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.

content.latin: Deus, in cuius passióne, secúndum Simeónis prophetíam, dulcíssimam ánimam gloriósæ Vírginis et Matris Maríæ dolóris gládius pertransívit: concéde propítius; ut, qui dolóres eius venerándo recólimus, passiónis tuæ efféctum felícem consequámur:
content.english: O God, at Whose suffering the prophecy of Simeon was fulfilled, and a sword of sorrow pierced through the gentle soul of the glorious Virgin and Mother Mary, mercifully grant that we who speak worshipfully of her woes, may obtain the saving purchase of thy suffering.

content.latin: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Rector potens, verax Deus,
content.english: O God of truth, O Lord of might,

content.latin: Qui témperas rerum vices,
content.english: Who orderest time and change aright,

content.latin: Splendóre mane illúminas,
content.english: Who send’st the early morning ray,

content.latin: Et ígnibus merídiem:
content.english: And light’st the glow of perfect day:

content.latin: Exstíngue flammas lítium,
content.english: Extinguish thou each sinful fire,

content.latin: Aufer calórem nóxium,
content.english: And banish every ill desire;

content.latin: Confer salútem córporum,
content.english: And while thou keep’st the body whole,

content.latin: Verámque pacem córdium.
content.english: Shed forth thy peace upon the soul.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Almighty Father, hear our cry,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, our Lord most High,

content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

Suscepísti me, Dómine: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo.

content.latin: Psalmus 40 [1]
content.english: Psalm 40 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 40

content.latin: 40:2 Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
content.english: 40:2 Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.

segments.t: Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.

content.latin: 40:3 Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum eius.
content.english: 40:3 The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.

segments.t: Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum eius.

content.latin: 40:4 Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.
content.english: 40:4 The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.

segments.t: Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.

content.latin: 40:5 Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: 40:5 I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

segments.t: Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.

content.latin: 40:6 Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?
content.english: 40:6 My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?

segments.t: Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?

content.latin: 40:7 Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
content.english: 40:7 And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.

segments.t: Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.

content.latin: 40:7 Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
content.english: 40:7 He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.

segments.t: Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.

content.latin: 40:8 Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
content.english: 40:8 All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.

segments.t: Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.

content.latin: 40:9 Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
content.english: 40:9 They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?

segments.t: Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?

content.latin: 40:10 Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
content.english: 40:10 For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.

segments.t: Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.

content.latin: 40:11 Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
content.english: 40:11 But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.

content.latin: 40:12 In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
content.english: 40:12 By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.

segments.t: In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.

content.latin: 40:13 Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
content.english: 40:13 But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

segments.t: Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.

content.latin: 40:14 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
content.english: 40:14 Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.

content.latin: 41:2 Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.
content.english: 41:2 As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; * so my soul panteth after thee, O God.

segments.t: Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.

content.latin: 41:3 Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
content.english: 41:3 My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

segments.t: Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?

content.latin: 41:4 Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
content.english: 41:4 My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?

segments.t: Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?

content.latin: 41:5 Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.
content.english: 41:5 These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: * for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:

segments.t: Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.

content.latin: 41:5 In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
content.english: 41:5 With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.

segments.t: In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.

content.latin: 41:6 Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:6 Why art thou sad, O my soul? * and why dost thou trouble me?

segments.t: Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?

content.latin: 41:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

segments.t: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 41(7-12)

content.latin: 41:7 Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.
content.english: 41:7 My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.

segments.t: Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.

content.latin: 41:8 Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.
content.english: 41:8 Deep calleth on deep, * at the noise of thy flood-gates.

segments.t: Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.

content.latin: 41:8 Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.
content.english: 41:8 All thy heights and thy billows * have passed over me.

segments.t: Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.

content.latin: 41:9 In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.
content.english: 41:9 In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.

segments.t: In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.

content.latin: 41:9 Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
content.english: 41:9 With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.

segments.t: Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.

content.latin: 41:10 Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
content.english: 41:10 Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?

segments.t: Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?

content.latin: 41:11 Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
content.english: 41:11 Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;

segments.t: Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.

content.latin: 41:11 Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?

content.latin: 43:2 Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.

content.latin: 43:3 Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
content.english: 43:3 Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and thou plantedst them: * thou didst afflict the people and cast them out.

segments.t: Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.

content.latin: 43:4 Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:

segments.t: Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.

content.english: 43:5 Thou art thyself my king and my God, * who commandest the saving of Jacob.

segments.t: Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Iacob.

content.latin: 43:6 In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.

segments.t: In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.

segments.t: Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.

content.latin: 43:8 Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.

segments.t: Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.

content.latin: 43:9 In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
content.english: 43:9 In God shall we glory all the day long: * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.

segments.t: Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.

content.english: 43:15 Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: * a shaking of the head among the people.

segments.t: A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.

content.latin: 43:18 Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.

content.english: Psalm 109 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 109

content.latin: 109:1 Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
content.english: 109:1 The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

segments.t: Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:

content.latin: 109:1 Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
content.english: 109:1 Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

segments.t: Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.

content.latin: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
content.english: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

segments.t: Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.

content.latin: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
content.english: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

segments.t: Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.

content.latin: 109:4 Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
content.english: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

segments.t: Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.

content.latin: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
content.english: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

segments.t: Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.

content.latin: 109:6 Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
content.english: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

segments.t: Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.

content.latin: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
content.english: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

segments.t: De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.

content.english: Psalm 112 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 112

content.latin: 112:1 Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.
content.english: 112:1 Praise the Lord, ye children: * praise ye the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 112:2 (fit reverentia) Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
content.english: 112:2 (bow head) Blessed be the name of the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.

segments.t: 112:2 (fit reverentia)
Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.

content.latin: 112:3 A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.
content.english: 112:3 From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, * the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

segments.t: A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 112:4 Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória eius.
content.english: 112:4 The Lord is high above all nations; * and his glory above the heavens.

segments.t: Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória eius.

content.latin: 112:5 Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?
content.english: 112:5 Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: * and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?

segments.t: Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?

content.latin: 112:7 Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:
content.english: 112:7 Raising up the needy from the earth, * and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:

segments.t: Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:

content.latin: 112:8 Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.
content.english: 112:8 That he may place him with princes, * with the princes of his people.

segments.t: Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.

content.latin: 112:9 Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.
content.english: 112:9 Who maketh a barren woman to dwell in a house, * the joyful mother of children.

segments.t: Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.

content.latin: Psalmus 121 [3]
content.english: Psalm 121 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 121

content.latin: 121:1 Lætátus sum in his, quæ dicta sunt mihi: * In domum Dómini íbimus.
content.english: 121:1 I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: * We shall go into the house of the Lord.

segments.t: Lætátus sum in his, quæ dicta sunt mihi: * In domum Dómini íbimus.

content.latin: 121:2 Stantes erant pedes nostri, * in átriis tuis, Ierúsalem.
content.english: 121:2 Our feet were standing * in thy courts, O Jerusalem.

segments.t: Stantes erant pedes nostri, * in átriis tuis, Ierúsalem.

content.latin: 121:3 Ierúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas: * cuius participátio eius in idípsum.
content.english: 121:3 Jerusalem, which is built as a city, * which is compact together.

segments.t: Ierúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas: * cuius participátio eius in idípsum.

content.latin: 121:4 Illuc enim ascendérunt tribus, tribus Dómini: * testimónium Israël ad confiténdum nómini Dómini.
content.english: 121:4 For thither did the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord: * the testimony of Israel, to praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Illuc enim ascendérunt tribus, tribus Dómini: * testimónium Israël ad confiténdum nómini Dómini.

content.latin: 121:5 Quia illic sedérunt sedes in iudício, * sedes super domum David.
content.english: 121:5 Because their seats have sat in judgment, * seats upon the house of David.

segments.t: Quia illic sedérunt sedes in iudício, * sedes super domum David.

content.latin: 121:6 Rogáte quæ ad pacem sunt Ierúsalem: * et abundántia diligéntibus te:
content.english: 121:6 Pray ye for the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem: * and abundance for them that love thee.

segments.t: Rogáte quæ ad pacem sunt Ierúsalem: * et abundántia diligéntibus te:

content.latin: 121:7 Fiat pax in virtúte tua: * et abundántia in túrribus tuis.
content.english: 121:7 Let peace be in thy strength: * and abundance in thy towers.

segments.t: Fiat pax in virtúte tua: * et abundántia in túrribus tuis.

content.latin: 121:8 Propter fratres meos, et próximos meos, * loquébar pacem de te:
content.english: 121:8 For the sake of my brethren, and of my neighbours, * I spoke peace of thee.

segments.t: Propter fratres meos, et próximos meos, * loquébar pacem de te:

content.latin: 121:9 Propter domum Dómini, Dei nostri, * quæsívi bona tibi.
content.english: 121:9 Because of the house of the Lord our God, * I have sought good things for thee.

segments.t: Propter domum Dómini, Dei nostri, * quæsívi bona tibi.

content.latin: 126:1 Nisi Dóminus ædificáverit domum, * in vanum laboravérunt qui ædíficant eam.
content.english: 126:1 Unless the Lord build the house, * they labour in vain that build it.

segments.t: Nisi Dóminus ædificáverit domum, * in vanum laboravérunt qui ædíficant eam.

content.latin: 126:1 Nisi Dóminus custodíerit civitátem, * frustra vígilat qui custódit eam.
content.english: 126:1 Unless the Lord keep the city, * he watcheth in vain that keepeth it.

segments.t: Nisi Dóminus custodíerit civitátem, * frustra vígilat qui custódit eam.

content.latin: 126:2 Vanum est vobis ante lucem súrgere: * súrgite postquam sedéritis, qui manducátis panem dolóris.
content.english: 126:2 It is vain for you to rise before light, * rise ye after you have sitten, you that eat the bread of sorrow.

segments.t: Vanum est vobis ante lucem súrgere: * súrgite postquam sedéritis, qui manducátis panem dolóris.

content.latin: 126:2 Cum déderit diléctis suis somnum: * ecce heréditas Dómini fílii: merces, fructus ventris.
content.english: 126:2 When he shall give sleep to his beloved, * behold the inheritance of the Lord are children: the reward, the fruit of the womb.

segments.t: Cum déderit diléctis suis somnum: * ecce heréditas Dómini fílii: merces, fructus ventris.

content.latin: 126:4 Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis: * ita fílii excussórum.
content.english: 126:4 As arrows in the hand of the mighty, * so the children of them that have been shaken.

segments.t: Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis: * ita fílii excussórum.

content.latin: 126:5 Beátus vir, qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis: * non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.
content.english: 126:5 Blessed is the man that hath filled the desire with them; * he shall not be confounded when he shall speak to his enemies in the gate.

segments.t: Beátus vir, qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis: * non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.

segments.t: Psalmus 147

content.latin: 147:1 Lauda, Ierúsalem, Dóminum: * lauda Deum tuum, Sion.
content.english: 147:1 Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem: * praise thy God, O Sion.

segments.t: Lauda, Ierúsalem, Dóminum: * lauda Deum tuum, Sion.

content.latin: 147:2 Quóniam confortávit seras portárum tuárum: * benedíxit fíliis tuis in te.
content.english: 147:2 Because he hath strengthened the bolts of thy gates * he hath blessed thy children within thee.

segments.t: Quóniam confortávit seras portárum tuárum: * benedíxit fíliis tuis in te.

content.latin: 147:3 Qui pósuit fines tuos pacem: * et ádipe fruménti sátiat te.
content.english: 147:3 Who hath placed peace in thy borders: * and filleth thee with the fat of corn.

segments.t: Qui pósuit fines tuos pacem: * et ádipe fruménti sátiat te.

content.latin: 147:4 Qui emíttit elóquium suum terræ: * velóciter currit sermo eius.
content.english: 147:4 Who sendeth forth his speech to the earth: * his word runneth swiftly.

segments.t: Qui emíttit elóquium suum terræ: * velóciter currit sermo eius.

content.latin: 147:5 Qui dat nivem sicut lanam: * nébulam sicut cínerem spargit.
content.english: 147:5 Who giveth snow like wool: * scattereth mists like ashes.

segments.t: Qui dat nivem sicut lanam: * nébulam sicut cínerem spargit.

content.latin: 147:6 Mittit crystállum suam sicut buccéllas: * ante fáciem frígoris eius quis sustinébit?
content.english: 147:6 He sendeth his crystal like morsels: * who shall stand before the face of his cold?

segments.t: Mittit crystállum suam sicut buccéllas: * ante fáciem frígoris eius quis sustinébit?

content.latin: 147:7 Emíttet verbum suum, et liquefáciet ea: * flabit spíritus eius, et fluent aquæ.
content.english: 147:7 He shall send out his word, and shall melt them: * his wind shall blow, and the waters shall run.

segments.t: Emíttet verbum suum, et liquefáciet ea: * flabit spíritus eius, et fluent aquæ.

content.latin: 147:8 Qui annúntiat verbum suum Iacob: * iustítias, et iudícia sua Israël.
content.english: 147:8 Who declareth his word to Jacob: * his justices and his judgments to Israel.

segments.t: Qui annúntiat verbum suum Iacob: * iustítias, et iudícia sua Israël.

content.latin: 147:9 Non fecit táliter omni natióni: * et iudícia sua non manifestávit eis.
content.english: 147:9 He hath not done in like manner to every nation: * and his judgments he hath not made manifest to them.

segments.t: Non fecit táliter omni natióni: * et iudícia sua non manifestávit eis.

content.english: Lam 2:13

segments.t: Lam 2:13

content.latin: Cui comparábo te? vel cui assimilábo te, fília Ierúsalem? cui exæquábo te, et consolábor te, virgo fília Sion? Magna est velut mare contrítio tua.
content.english: To what shall I compare thee? or to what shall I liken thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? to what shall I equal thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Sion? for great as the sea is thy destruction: who shall heal thee?

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: Hymnus
content.english: Hymn

segments.t: Hymnus

content.latin: Iam toto súbitus vesper eat polo,
content.english: Now let the darkling eve mount suddenly on high,

content.latin: Et sol attónitum præcípitet diem,
content.english: The sun affrighted reave his splendours from the sky,

content.latin: Dum sævæ récolo ludíbrium necis,
content.english: While I in silence grieve o'er the mocked agony

content.latin: Divinámque catástrophen.
content.english: And the divine catastrophe.

content.latin: Spectátrix áderas supplício, Parens,
content.english: Grief-drenched, thou dost appear with heart of adamant,

content.latin: Malis uda, gerens cor adamántinum;
content.english: O Mother; and dost hear the great hierophant,

content.latin: Natus funérea péndulus in cruce
content.english: Upon his wooden bier locked in the arms of death,

content.latin: Altos dum gémitus dabat.
content.english: Utter in groans his parting breath.

content.latin: Pendens ante óculos Natus, atrócibus
content.english: What lookest thou upon, mangled and bruised and torn?

content.latin: Sectus verbéribus, Natus hiántibus
content.english: Ah, 'tis the very Son thy yearning breast hath borne!

content.latin: Fossus vulnéribus, quot penetrántibus
content.english: Surely, each breaking moan and each deep-mouthèd wound

content.latin: Te confíxit acúleis!
content.english: Its fellow in thy heart hath found!

content.latin: Eheu! Sputa, álapæ, vérbera, vúlnera,
content.english: Surely, the taunts and woes, the scourge, the dripping thorn,

content.latin: Clavi, fel, áloë, spóngia, láncea,
content.english: The spitting and the blows, the gall, the lance, the scorn—

content.latin: Sitis, spina, cruor, quam vária pium
content.english: Surely, each torment throws a poison-dart at thee,

content.latin: Cor pressére tyránnide!
content.english: Crushed by their manifold tyranny.

content.latin: Cunctis intérea stas generósior,
content.english: Yet thou with patient mien beneath his cross dost stand,

content.latin: Virgo, Martýribus: prodígio novo,
content.english: Nobler in this, I ween, than all the martyr-band:

content.latin: In tantis móriens non móreris, Parens,
content.english: A thousand deaths, O Queen, upon thy spirit lie,

content.latin: Diris fixa dolóribus.
content.english: Yet thou, O marvel! dost not die.

content.latin: Sit summæ Tríadi glória, laus, honor,

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: percutit sibi pectus mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ídeo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, et omnes Sanctos, oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
content.english: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: strikes his breast through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

segments.t: Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis eius sperábis.

content.latin: 133:1 Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.
content.english: 133:1 Who stand in the house of the Lord, * in the courts of the house of our God.

segments.t: Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.

content.latin: 133:2 In nóctibus extóllite manus vestras in sancta, * et benedícite Dóminum.
content.english: 133:2 In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, * and bless ye the Lord.

segments.t: In nóctibus extóllite manus vestras in sancta, * et benedícite Dóminum.

content.latin: 133:3 Benedícat te Dóminus ex Sion, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
content.english: 133:3 May the Lord out of Sion bless thee, * he that made heaven and earth.

segments.t: Benedícat te Dóminus ex Sion, * qui fecit cælum et terram.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Miserére mihi, Dómine, et exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: Ant. Have mercy on me, O Lord, and hear my prayer.

segments.t: Ant.
Miserére mihi, Dómine, et exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: Te lucis ante términum,
content.english: Before the ending of the day,

content.latin: Rerum Creátor, póscimus,
content.english: Creator of the world, we pray

content.latin: Ut pro tua cleméntia
content.english: That with thy wonted favor thou

content.latin: Sis præsul et custódia.
content.english: Wouldst be our guard and keeper now.

content.latin: Procul recédant sómnia,
content.english: From all ill dreams defend our eyes,

content.latin: Et nóctium phantásmata;
content.english: From nightly fears and fantasies;

content.latin: Hostémque nostrum cómprime,
content.english: Tread under foot our ghostly foe,

content.latin: Ne polluántur córpora.
content.english: That no pollution we may know.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: O Father, that we ask be done,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.english: Jer 14:9

content.latin: Tu autem in nobis es, Dómine, et nomen sanctum tuum invocátum est super nos: ne derelínquas nos, Dómine, Deus noster.
content.english: But thou, O Lord, art among us, and thy name is called upon by us: forsake us not, O Lord our God.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℣. Redemísti nos, Dómine, Deus veritátis.

content.latin: ℣. Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi.
content.english: ℣. Keep us, Lord, as the apple of thine eye.

segments.t: Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi.

content.latin: ℟. Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos.
content.english: ℟. Protect us under the shadow of thy wings.

segments.t: Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos.

content.latin: Ant. Salva nos, * Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.
content.english: Ant. Protect us, * Lord, while we are awake and safeguard us while we sleep; that we may keep watch with Christ, and rest in peace.

segments.t: Ant.
Salva nos, * Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.

content.latin: 2:29 Nunc dimíttis ✠ servum tuum, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum in pace:
content.english: 2:29 Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, ✠ * according to thy word in peace;

segments.t: Nunc dimíttis ✠ servum tuum, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum in pace:

content.latin: 2:30 Quia vidérunt óculi mei * salutáre tuum,
content.english: 2:30 Because my eyes have seen * thy salvation,

segments.t: Quia vidérunt óculi mei * salutáre tuum,

content.latin: 2:31 Quod parásti * ante fáciem ómnium populórum,
content.english: 2:31 Which thou hast prepared * before the face of all peoples:

content.latin: 2:32 Lumen ad revelatiónem géntium, * et glóriam plebis tuæ Israël.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Vísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: Ángeli tui sancti hábitent in ea, qui nos in pace custódiant; et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
content.english: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.
content.english: Benediction. The almighty and merciful Lord, ✠ the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, bless us and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ;
content.english: Hail holy Queen, Mother of Mercy,

content.latin: vita, dulcédo et spes nóstra, salve.
content.english: our life, our sweetness, and our hope.

content.latin: Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ.
content.english: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

content.latin: Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes
content.english: To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping

content.latin: In hac lacrimárum valle.
content.english: In this valley of tears.

content.latin: Eia ergo, advocáta nostra,
content.english: Turn then, most gracious Advocate,

content.latin: illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte.
content.english: thine eyes of mercy toward us.

content.latin: Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui,
content.english: And after this our exile show unto us

content.latin: nobis post hoc exsílium osténde.
content.english: the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

content.latin: O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo María.
content.english: O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

content.latin: ℣. Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.
content.english: ℣. Pray for us, O Holy Mother of God.

segments.t: Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.

content.latin: ℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
content.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

segments.t: Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui gloriósæ Vírginis Matris Maríæ corpus et ánimam, ut dignum Fílii tui habitáculum éffici mererétur, Spíritu Sancto cooperánte, præparásti: da, ut, cuius commemoratióne lætámur, eius pia intercessióne, ab instántibus malis et a morte perpétua liberémur. Per eúndem Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
content.english: O almighty, everlasting God, who by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, didst prepare the body and soul of Mary, glorious Virgin and Mother, to become a worthy dwelling for Thy Son; grant that we who rejoice in her commemoration may, by her gracious intercession, be delivered from present evils and from everlasting death. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.
content.english: ℣. May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.

segments.t: Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.
